task: Per-residue P1 protease cleavage-site probability for a candidate peptide (substrate), against a bundled panel of 6,460 enzymes (proteases).
architecture: UniZyme Transformer_DE: one encoder layer per side (2 heads, d_model 480, Gaussian distance kernels, K=10); the enzyme side also takes a residue frustration matrix; an active-site head feeds a pooled concatenation MLP that scores each substrate residue. See architecture.py.

inference_inputs_required.sequence: candidate peptide amino-acid sequence, standard 20 AAs, at most 1500 residues
inference_inputs_required.enzyme_accession: UniProt accession of a bundled enzyme (see enzymes/enzyme_catalog.csv), or omit to score against the full panel via predict()
inference_inputs_required.distance_matrix: optional (len(sequence), len(sequence)) float array, pairwise C-alpha distance in Angstroms; when omitted the peptide is folded with ESMFold

enzyme_panel_selection: Every enzyme in UniZyme's data with a structure and a frustration matrix: 542 MEROPS-keyed training enzymes, 5,886 pretraining enzymes and 32 added for the wound-healing and metabolic pipelines. Ten wound-allowlist matrices were computed with frustratometer (configurational, k_electrostatics 0, min separation 12); the rest are UniZyme's own.
known_limits: CLEAVAGE_PROB_THRESHOLD is 0.5 and has not been calibrated; no precision/recall was measured for this checkpoint on peptides.
Ten of the energy matrices were computed locally rather than taken from UniZyme.
Energy matrices are stored as float16 (predictions differ by at most about 1e-4 from float32).
predict() requires the enzymes to be named; the panel is too large to screen in full.
Matrices are zero-padded to 1500 residues as in the original code, so inference cost does not scale down with peptide length.

enzymes_screened_by_pipelines.wound_healing: the 33 accessions in WOUND_PROTEASE_ACCESSIONS (pipeline/s08_safety_developability/stage.py), all in the panel
